TowerTorch can hand its alerts to TollRoll, takes over the folders of another folder plugin and shows an app's logo where a container has no icon. It also makes room for FolderView Plus, Unassigned Devices Next and dlandon's plugins, and theming off or an area switch takes its look away completely.

## ✨ Added

- **TollRoll can send TowerTorch's alerts.** While TollRoll is the notification hub of your fortress, TowerTorch hands it every alert and the summary of the maintenance plan, so TollRoll's quiet hours, daily summary and limits apply to them as well. The Notifications card says so while it does. Without TollRoll, or with its hub switched off, TowerTorch sends to Unraid and the webhook itself.
- **The watchdog tells you when a container runs again.** If the watchdog gave up on a container or could not restart it, an alert follows once the container is running again. Through TollRoll it also reaches a channel set to Only problems.
- **Take over the folders of another folder plugin.** When another folder plugin keeps Docker folders, the gear menu on the Docker tab offers Take over folders. A preview shows which containers land in which folder before anything is created, and each folder keeps its colour. Folders that already exist and containers already in a folder stay as they are, so a second run changes nothing. The other plugin's files are left untouched.
- **Logos for containers without an icon.** Where Unraid shows its question mark, the Docker tab shows the logo of the app the container runs, coloured in your icon style. TowerTorch knows the app by the container's image, and by its name only when the image gives nothing away. 70 logos ship with the plugin, so they show without internet too. Only the display changes, the template stays as it is, and the App logos card on the Docker tab of the settings turns them off.
- **The icon search knows a container by its image.** A container with an icon of its own is looked up by the app its image runs as well, so one you gave a name of your own still finds its brand logo. An icon you set yourself is never swapped.
- **State colours off.** A switch in the Badges card gives every state indicator the accent colour instead of green, orange and red: status badges, state dots, usage bars, the header chips and the dots and chips in the maintenance window. Plugins that take TowerTorch's colours follow, ShipLog's chips among them, and the tooltip still says what a state means.
- **Home and End open a dropdown at either end.** On a closed dropdown they open it on its first or last option. The dropdowns in the container form, on the share pages, in the limits window and on the settings page also take the arrow keys, Enter, Space and Escape once open.
- **Discord on the Help card.** The card offers GitHub, the TowerTorch Discord server and the bug report. The mail button is gone.

## 🎨 Design

- **GlimStone 4.9.2.** Quiet buttons, segments, rows, menu entries and dropdown options light in a soft tint of your accent under the pointer, where they used to step to grey. FireSquire, ShipLog and TollRoll read the same hover colour from TowerTorch, so all four light alike.
- **Open dropdowns are plain rows.** Their entries are no longer chips filled with the accent. The entry under the pointer or the keyboard gets the soft tint, and the chosen one stands in bold with GlimStone's check. A dropdown you reach with Tab shows it with a step in its fill, like the text fields beside it.
- **A focus ring you can see.** Keyboard focus is a solid ring in the accent's ink instead of a faint halo, 2px wide and 3px when your system asks for more contrast.
- **A deeper accent ink on the light themes.** Text, links and glyphs in the accent reach 4.5:1 on every card, and a colour you picked yourself still gets its own ink where it would be too faint.
- **Placeholders you can read.** The hint in an empty field reaches 4.5:1 on every background.
- **Soft corners from the start.** If you never picked a shape, TowerTorch starts on GlimStone's soft corners, pictures included, and FireSquire and ShipLog follow. Round stays a choice of its own, and a shape you picked is kept.
- **Reactive buttons keep their width.** In reactive mode a button is as wide as with its glyph and words, and the words open inside it, so in a wrapping row it no longer slips away from the pointer. The login button keeps one width in every label mode.
- **Version and Components cards on the Info tab.** The Version card shows TowerTorch's number with one line on where its updates stand, and says Not checked yet until Unraid has looked. The engine and GlimStone move to a Components card of their own, and each number opens its project's newest release. Every number is a 24px target, and on a phone a long number or status moves to a line of its own. On Unraid's light themes the buttons and the update line stay readable on the dark card.
- **The User Scripts list uses the whole width.** Names and descriptions get the room, the buttons stand in even columns from row to row, and in a narrow window they move below the name.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The update check asks Unraid.** Check for updates on the Info tab runs the same check as the Plugins tab, so the two never disagree. While a new version waits, What's new opens its notes and a button leads to the Plugins tab, where Unraid installs it.
- **Each area switch takes its whole look away.** Turn off Docker, Plugins, VMs, Main, Shares, the header area, Settings or Favorites under Areas, and that area's pages look the way Unraid draws them, tab strips, title bars and table heads included. Every other area keeps its look. With the Docker area off, TowerTorch's Docker functions keep working, as with theming off. Thanks @Revan335 for the idea ([#136](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/136)).
- **Space ticks a container in a plan, Enter no longer does**, the way a native checkbox behaves.
- **ParleyPort 1.3.8.** The fortress parts come from ParleyPort. Your fortress membership, notification channels and settings carry over as they are.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A right-click on a menu tab opens the browser's menu.** On Linux and macOS a plain right-click anywhere in the webGUI, such as on a tab in the menu bar, opens the browser's own menu, so a tab can be opened in a new tab or its link copied. Before, the right-button wheel gesture kept the menu shut. On Windows that gesture still scrolls a row sideways, and Shift with the wheel does it everywhere. Thanks @Revan335 ([#139](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/139)).
- **The (i) icons open on a click.** A click or a tap on an (i), on TowerTorch's own settings and on every Settings and Tools page, opens its help and keeps it open until you click somewhere else. Before, the click closed the bubble the hover had just opened. Thanks @Revan335 ([#138](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/138)).
- **Theming off turns the whole look off.** The Docker and Plugins tabs kept TowerTorch's tabs, title bars and action bar, and the Wild motion level still made Unraid's menu bounce. With theming off, Unraid looks like plain Unraid, and the Docker functions keep working. Thanks @Revan335 ([#136](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/136)).
- **A yes/no switch keeps a plugin's settings.** On a plugin's settings page, such as Folder Caching, Recycle Bin, File Activity, Tips and Tweaks, Enhanced Log or Unassigned Devices, flipping a switch could reset that plugin's other settings and skip the restart its Apply runs. There the switch waits for Apply, and Unraid's own display settings still save at once. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **FolderView Plus keeps its folders.** A click on a folder row opens its menu again, the folder autostart switch works, and TowerTorch's grid, folder and tile views, the page search and the Dashboard order leave FolderView Plus's folders where it puts them. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **Unassigned Devices Next looks right.** Its renamed tables and headings get the TowerTorch look again, the gear and refresh sit in the controls card, the historical devices join the tile row, and each switch shows one tooltip. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **Recycle Bin Next and File Activity Next** show their status as a dot beside the page title, and their log filters sit in a plain row instead of one large badge. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **ZFS Master NG's dataset table** is no longer treated like the array table. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **Preclear stays in its place.** Its status stays out of a disk tile's serial number, and its footer icons stay on screen while a preclear runs with the footer hidden. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **A plugin's own menu tab**, such as Custom SMB Shares, keeps its name with the tabs set to icons only. Thanks @Revan335 ([#135](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues/135)).
- **Light themes.** Other plugins' tables on Tools and Settings pages, the list of the dropdown on the settings page, the header bell and the (i) icons on Main are readable again.
- **The heading on the Settings and Tools pages reads on the dark themes.** The page name in the accent badge takes the badge's dark ink, and the page's own symbol shows in front of it again.
- **Update windows wait for the download.** When you updated a container or a plugin, the progress window could show its tick and Done from the start, carried over from the window before it. Every window starts with the loading ring and shows the tick only once the job is finished.
- **The arrow on a script category's tile follows your icon style.** It stayed white and vanished on a light accent such as yellow. It takes the tile's ink, black on yellow.
- **A brand glyph no longer shows in plain black.** With Tint icons off, a known app's one-colour glyph could replace its logo and stay black. The logo stays in that case.
- **A maintenance job reaches the backup app while it reconnects, and starts only once.** If the backup app had just joined again or changed its name, the job could fail, and a request whose answer got lost could start it twice.
- **Apps of your fortress on a server with a single network find each other at home directly** instead of only through the relay.
- **A phrase change counts every app that took it.** An app whose answer got lost on the way back was listed as gone, although it had the new phrase.
- **A restart no longer keeps two apps apart.** If an app of your fortress restarted while a new one was joining, the two never learned which app the other was. The newcomer asks again.
- **Security fixes for the fortress.** A member's direct call can no longer be steered to another page on a host it reaches, oversized messages are turned away before they take up memory, and golang.org/x/net 0.63.0 brings the latest fixes to Go's network library.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Everything new is in German and English**, like the rest of TowerTorch.
